claim: Under GBL § 396-b, a synthetic performer is a digitally created asset created, reproduced or modified by computer using generative AI or a software algorithm.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: "Synthetic performer" means a digitally created asset created, reproduced, or modified by computer,

claim: A synthetic performer is intended to create the impression of a human performer who is not recognizable as any identifiable natural performer.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: who is not recognizable as any identifiable natural performer.

claim: The disclosure duty applies to any person in the business of dealing in property or services who, for any commercial purpose, produces or creates an advertisement.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: Any person engaged in the business of dealing in any property or service who for any commercial purpose produces or creates an advertisement
verifier_note: Added the statute's 'for any commercial purpose' condition, omitted in the draft.

claim: Such a person must conspicuously disclose in the advertisement that a synthetic performer is in it.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: shall conspicuously disclose in such advertisement that a synthetic performer is in such advertisement,

claim: The disclosure duty applies where the person has actual knowledge.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: where such person has actual knowledge.

claim: A first violation carries a civil penalty of $1,000.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: A violation of this subdivision shall result in a civil penalty of one thousand dollars for a first violation,

claim: Each subsequent violation carries a civil penalty of $5,000.
publisher: New York State Senate (nysenate.gov), General Business Law § 396-B
evidence: and five thousand dollars for any subsequent violation.
